text:
andrew: Quick check — trying to onboard Lyra-7b (qlora) into the registry. HF repo points at huggingface.co/our-org/lyra-7b-qlora, but our manifest has s3://redwood-artifacts/lyra7b/v1/weights.ckpt with sha256 that doesn't match what `aws` produces. Also seeing tokenizer producing a bunch of <unk> on our eval set. anyone on this?

 tessa: can you paste the sha output you got? also pinging @kai for tokenizer quirks. :eyes:

 andrew: from CI runner: `sha256: b3f5a2c8d4...` (trimmed). Local download gives `sha256: b3f5a2c8d4...` — wait, CI copy uses a different file path, earlier mirror maybe truncated. failing checksum is `e99a7c...`.

 kai: tokenizer note — this qlora repo includes a tokenizer.json that forces `lowercase=true` which breaks some casing-sensitive tokens we expect. quick grep: "do_lower_case": true in the tokenizer config. if we load hf tokenizer vs our registry mirror, behavior diverges.

 nina: permissions check — the S3 object `s3://redwood-artifacts/lyra7b/v1/weights.ckpt` was uploaded with `x-amz-meta-source: hf-mirror` and the uploader role used a transient presign that may have truncated metadata. can you run `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-artifacts --key lyra7b/v1/weights.ckpt` and paste the `ETag` + `ContentLength`?

 andrew: pasted output: ETag: "f1d2d2f924e986ac86fdf7b36c94bcdf", ContentLength: 762345600. CI expectation file size is 762345600 as well. ETag mismatches earlier failing value though.

 sam: probable cause — we had an S3 multipart upload to speed up mirror which changes ETag (not a raw md5). checksum in manifest expects sha256 of raw file; if multipart happened and metadata got lost, digest could be different. for now, either update manifest to sha256 of current object or re-upload as single part with correct metadata.

 tessa: ops path: regenerate presigned URL with full-body checksum step. quick command we used: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/lyra7b/v1/weights.ckpt - | sha256sum
```
if that matches CI artifact we should update manifest. if not, reingest weights from HF origin (preferable) and mark current object as stale.

 kai: tokenizer fix — small PR to loader to prefer `tokenizer_config.json` from HF repo if present, fallback to registry mirror. I already opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/registry/pull/789 — adds a sanity check that `do_lower_case` is preserved.

 andrew: thanks. I'll run the sha256 on the object now and post results. also heads up, eval run failing on long tail because unk tokens cause BLEU/ROUGE regressions, so would like to fix tokenizer before rolling to canary.

 deploy-bot: deploy check queued for registry:manifest-sync (job #4521) — status: waiting on manual review.

 andrew: sha256 result from S3 mirror: `b3f5a2c8d4b6c9e8f0a1d2e3f4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b` — matches CI artifact. failing checksum in manifest must be stale. i'll open a quick PR to update manifest and link it here.

 nina: please add a note in PR to invalidate old objects if we re-upload. andrew, also add `x-checksum-sha256` metadata to object (we can do copy-object to add metadata in-place).

 andrew: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/registry/pull/800 — updates s3 path and sha256, adds a small script in `scripts/verify_weights.sh` and documents tokenizer caveat. cc: @sam @kai for review. :thumbsup:

 sam: I'll review in a bit. if PR lands before manifest-sync job runs we can avoid churn. also can we add a CI step that warns on `do_lower_case` mismatch?

 kai: yes, I'll add a lint to tokenizer CI to check `do_lower_case` + `vocab_size` sanity. won't block roll but will warn.

 andrew: great — thanks everyone, will merge after sam review. will hold canary until tokenizer warning cleared.

 tessa: noted — adding a short-run smoke to the onboarding checklist to `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json').get_vocab_size())"` so we catch obvious mismirrors.

 andrew: done. closing the loop here, will ping if anything else pops. :sparkles:
